summary.headline: IIFL Finance Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 93% YoY to INR805 crore, first quarter above INR800 crore, with AUM up 38% YoY to INR1,24,268 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated loan AUM grew 8% QoQ and 38% YoY to INR1,24,268 crore, with gold loans about 53% of the book. PAT of INR805 crore rose 13% QoQ, H1 PAT was about INR1,518 crore, and consolidated ROE was 20.1% annualised for H1. Gross NPA eased 7 bps QoQ to 1.48%, though gold-loan GNPA rose, and management said it will raise equity of 10-20% dilution at the listed parent, timing and investor type still open. Insurance commission regulation is a flagged headwind, estimated at about 5% of PBT.

financial_highlights.metric: Portfolio yield / cost of borrowing / spread
financial_highlights.change: yield -3 bps, CoB +3 bps, spread -6 bps QoQ

segments.name: Standalone (gold and LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM INR70,382 crore, 97% secured, gold about 93% of standalone AUM. NII +21% QoQ, PAT INR548.5 crore; yield 18.6% (+12 bps), spread 9.2% (+11 bps).

segments.name: IIFL Home Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR43,070 crore, disbursements INR3,498 crore (+10% QoQ), PPOP INR330 crore (+6% QoQ). Affordable disbursements about INR790 crore in Q2 vs INR400 crore in Q1; affordable yield about 12.5-12.6%, emerging under 0.5%.

segments.name: Samasta Finance (MFI)
segments.commentary: AUM INR10,816 crore, flat. GNPA 2.82% (-46 bps), PAT INR69 crore (+13% QoQ). September disbursements about INR550 crore, October target about INR800 crore, exit run-rate about INR1,000 crore/month by Feb-Mar.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged per management: about 25% AUM growth, similar profit growth, ROE of about 20% at upper end; management said it is on track to meet and exceed.
Consolidated ROE expected above 20% in the medium to long term; standalone ROE may dip temporarily post equity raise.
FY27 ROA for the group expected to be around breakeven to slightly positive given MSME/LAP repricing; target of 2.5-3% ROA next year.
Home finance AUM growth guided at 18-20%; ROE target of 16-18% for home finance next year.
Equity raise of 10-20% dilution targeted, with management aiming to close within the current quarter.
Insurance commission regime: consolidated PBT impact about 5% vs earlier 10% estimate; effective date may slip beyond 1 April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold GNPA rise about 30 bps QoQ, and what would a 10% gold price fall do?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects small-ticket customers paying late; the 90+ cohort LTV is about 85%. A 10% fall could lift NPAs to 1-3% but losses would stay minimal.

qa_highlights.question: How big and when is the standalone equity raise?
qa_highlights.answer: Board and shareholder approval already obtained; structure (PE or QIP) undecided, aim to close this quarter, dilution 10-20%. No subsidiary fundraise planned; parent raise via subsidiary stake sale or primary issue considered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is off-book income falling while off-book AUM rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending carries no upfront income and DA assignment income amortises; management expects NII to hold while upfront income declines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance commission impact?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 insurance income about INR240-250 crore, about 10% of PBT; now estimated about 5% PBT impact, with HFC about INR150-160 crore and Samasta about INR75-80 crore. Microfinance commission falls from about 14% to 3.5-5% under the draft.

qa_highlights.question: Why are home loan and MSME yields falling while GNPA declines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a deliberate shift to higher-quality borrowers, with lower yield, lower credit cost and collection cost; some high-yield micro-LAP and BLC pools are running off.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the home loan portfolio yield (about 10.4%) below disbursement yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited high-yield runoff pools and possible interest reversal; a reconciliation was to be checked offline.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility: a sharp fall could raise gold NPAs and auctions; auctions cited at about 1-2% of accounts per year.
Equity dilution of 10-20% and valuation; a shareholder pressed for a floor on price-to-book.
Insurance commission draft could cut group PBT by about 5%, with timing deferred beyond April and unclear mitigation.
Home finance yield compression and slow core home loan growth; mix change still unexplained in part.
Gold tonnage and yield held in competitive market ahead of festive season; tax demand under litigation with no update.
Co-lending/assignment economics; RBI rules on assignment and PSL treatment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and profitability, but defensive on gold NPAs, auctions, home loan yields and the timing and valuation of the equity raise. Management gave specific numbers where asked and deferred some questions offline.
key_quotes: So our strategy remains resilient capital-efficient growth and that's based on 6 pillars.
Hopefully, this quarter, we should be able to close something.
So you know our market cap. So dilution will be anywhere from 10% to 20%.
To tell you candidly, we don't have enough capital and we need -- so our capital adequacy is not adequate to meet -- to keep everything on the books.
capex_capacity: Standalone equity raise: board and shareholder approval already obtained last quarter; structure (PE or QIP) undecided; target to close within the current quarter; dilution 10-20% depending on investors.

No fundraise planned at subsidiary level (Home Finance, Samasta); parent raise could come via partial or full sale of a subsidiary or a primary raise; divestment expected to take time, so equity raise needed meanwhile. Management said no plan currently for IPO/stake sale of HFC or Samasta.

Branch network: 38 new branches added in home finance, taking count from about 311 to about 350, all in affordable segment; group has more than 5,000 branches; gold business added new branches over the last 2 quarters.

Liquidity of INR13,805 crore (cash and undrawn lines) at group level; standalone capital adequacy 17.03%, gearing 4.7x; consolidated CRAR 23.5%, gearing 4.1x; management said capital adequacy is not adequate to keep all co-lending volumes on book.

Off-book AUM INR42,796 crore (34% of AUM) across 18 banking co-lending/assignment partners; more than INR1.7 lakh crore originated over 10 years via assignment or co-lending; co-lending to scale up with newer bank relationships.
Home finance: management described gradual reorientation toward affordable housing; LAP target of 20-25% of the home finance book; growth catch-up expected in H2.
Samasta: microfinance disbursement about INR550 crore in September, targeted about INR800 crore in October, exit run-rate about INR1,000 crore a month by Feb-Mar.
demand_pricing: Consolidated AUM INR1,24,268 crore, +8% QoQ, +38% YoY; core businesses (gold, home, MSME, microfinance) about 97% of portfolio, +43% YoY.

Gold loans about 53% of consolidated portfolio; standalone gold about 93% of standalone AUM; management said market is expanding (higher gold prices lifting borrowing capacity, tighter unsecured/MFI lending pushing customers to gold) but competitive intensity is rising, with no yield cut to chase share. Gold tonnage rose from 64 to 69 tonnes per an analyst's figure (not disputed by management).

Gold GNPA rose about 30 bps QoQ per analyst; management attributed it to small-ticket customers paying late. 90+ DPD gold cohort LTV about 85%. Auctions about 1-2% of accounts per year; management said auctions were near zero in the prior 2-3 quarters. Income-generating gold loans started last quarter; about 20-25% of the book under that process.

Home finance disbursements (as reported on clearance basis) INR3,498 crore, +10% QoQ; management cited booking-basis disbursements of over INR4,000 crore, +41% QoQ; affordable disbursements about INR790 crore in Q2 vs INR400 crore in Q1; emerging segment disbursement yield below 0.5%, affordable blended yield about 12.5-12.6%. Incremental home loan disbursement yield 11.81% in Q2 per management; portfolio home loan yield about 10.4%, down 10 bps QoQ, which management attributed to runoff of high-yield micro-LAP and BLC pools; reconciliation with disbursement yield left partly unresolved.
Home finance AUM growth about 8% YoY per management; guidance of 18-20% AUM growth retained; ROE target 16-18% for next year.

MSME/LAP yields fell about 98 bps QoQ per analyst; management said new micro-LAP business is priced at about 12.5-13.5% versus earlier micro-LAP yields of up to 34%, a deliberate shift to higher-quality borrowers that lowers credit and collection costs.
Standalone yield 18.6% (+12 bps QoQ), spread 9.2% (+11 bps). Consolidated portfolio yield 16.5% (-3 bps), CoB 9.08% (+3 bps), spread 7.42% (-6 bps).
Microfinance: insurance commission falling from about 14% to 3.5-5% under the draft; management said MFI growth muted in drought-hit geographies, expecting momentum to build in the festive season.
Co-lending on gold: about 40% of gold output portfolio is co-lent; management said co-lending carries no upfront income, so off-book income will decline while NII holds.

adds.what: 38 new affordable-segment branches in IIFL Home Finance, taking count from about 311 to about 350

growth.why: FY27 guidance of about 25% AUM growth and similar profit growth is held, backed by consolidated AUM +38% YoY, gold book growth, 38 new home-finance branches and off-book co-lending with 18 bank partners, though capital adequacy is noted as insufficient to keep all co-lending on book and the equity raise and insurance headwind are still open.
